5. // Modules

8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9.

24.         Address,
25.         PageAligned,
26.         PhysicalAddress,
27.         TruncatedMemoryRegion,
28.         VirtualAddress,
29.     },
30.     mm::phys::upool::Upool,
31. };
32. use ::alloc::collections::LinkedList;
33. use ::arch::mem;
34. use ::bitmap::Bitmap;
35. use ::sys::error::Error;
36. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
37. use ::vstd::prelude::*;
38. 
39. // Include specifications.
40. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
41. include!("mod.spec.rs");
42. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
43. include!("mod.proof.rs");
44. 
45. //==================================================================================================
46. // Exports
47. //==================================================================================================
48. 
49. pub use self::{
50.     kframe::KernelFrame,
51.     manager::PhysMemoryManager,
52.     upool::UserFrame,
53. };
54. 
55. //==================================================================================================
56. // Standalone Functions
57. //==================================================================================================
58. 
59. // This function iterates the supplied `LinkedList` of regions. The std `LinkedList`
60. // iterator cannot be given a Verus `for`-loop specification from this crate (the orphan
61. // rule forbids implementing vstd's iterator traits for the foreign `Iter` type, and the
62. // pinned `vstd` dependency cannot be extended — see `mod.spec.rs` / `verus-unsupported.md`).
63. // The function is therefore `external_body`; its `#[verus_spec]` contract is honored by the
64. // caller (`init`). The abstract effect — every frame of every region becomes booked — is
65. // modelled by `PhysMemView::spec_book_frames` / `region_frames` and discharged by
66. // `lemma_book_region_reserves_region_frames` in `mod.proof.rs`. Because the region frames are
67. // the contents of the (un-viewable) `LinkedList`, they cannot be enumerated in this boundary
68. // contract; what is expressed is the caller-relevant guarantee that the allocator stays
69. // initialized and well-formed across booking.
70. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
71. #[verus_spec(result =>
72.     requires
73.         phys_view().initialized,
74.         phys_view().inv(),
75.     ensures
76.         phys_view().inv(),
77.         match result {
78.             Ok(()) => phys_view().initialized,
79.             Err(_) => true,
80.         },
81. )]
82. fn book_physical_memory_regions(
83.     physical_memory_regions: LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>>,
84. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
85.     info!("booking physical memory regions ...");
86. 
87.     // Book physical memory that is not usable.
88.     for region in physical_memory_regions.iter() {
89.         info!("booking: {:?}", region);
90.         frame::alloc_range(region)?;
91.     }
92. 
93.     Ok(())
94. }
95. 
96. // `external_body` for the same std-`LinkedList` reason as
97. // `book_physical_memory_regions`; its `#[verus_spec]` contract is honored by the caller
98. // (`init`). The abstract effect — every *tracked* MMIO frame (`is_covered`) becomes booked
99. // while untracked frames are skipped — is modelled by `PhysMemView::spec_book_frames` over
100. // `M.intersect(covered())` and discharged by `lemma_book_mmio_skip_untracked` /
101. // `lemma_book_mmio_books_tracked` in `mod.proof.rs`. As with the physical-region helper, the
102. // concrete MMIO frame set is the contents of the (un-viewable) `LinkedList`, so the boundary
103. // contract expresses the caller-relevant guarantee: the allocator stays initialized and
104. // well-formed (the skip-if-not-covered tolerance never aborts boot).
105. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
106. #[verus_spec(result =>
107.     requires
108.         phys_view().initialized,
109.         phys_view().inv(),
110.     ensures
111.         phys_view().inv(),
112.         match result {
113.             Ok(()) => phys_view().initialized,
114.             Err(_) => true,
115.         },
116. )]
117. fn book_mmio_regions(
118.     mmio_regions: &LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<VirtualAddress>>,
119. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
120.     info!("booking memory-mapped i/o regions ...");
121. 
122.     // Book memory-mapped I/O regions.
123.     for region in mmio_regions.iter() {
124.         info!("booking: {:?}", region);
125.         let mut start: usize = region.start().into_raw_value();
126.         let end: usize = start + (region.size() - 1);
127.         while start < end {
128.             let mmio_addr: usize = crate::hal::platform::gva_to_gpa(start);
129.             let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> = PageAligned::from_address(unsafe {
130.                 // MMIO GPAs may legitimately lie outside tracked RAM, so they must not go through
131.                 // the regular physical-address validator here.
132.                 PhysicalAddress::from_mmio_address(VirtualAddress::from_raw_value(mmio_addr))?
133.             })?;
134. 
135.             // Only book frames that the frame allocator actually tracks.
136.             // MMIO regions above RAM (e.g. the LAPIC at 0xFEE0_0000) are not
137.             // covered by the bitmap and must be skipped.
138.             if frame::is_covered(phys_addr) {
139.                 frame::book(phys_addr)?;
140.             }
141.             start += mem::FRAME_SIZE;
142.         }
143.     }
144. 
145.     Ok(())
146. }
147. 
148. ///
149. /// # Description
150. ///
151. /// Initializes the physical memory manager.
152. ///
153. /// # Parameters
154. ///
155. /// - `physical_memory_regions`: Physical memory regions to book.
156. /// - `mmio_regions`: Memory-mapped I/O regions to book.
157. /// - `physical_memory_layout`: Physical memory layout bitmap.
158. ///
159. /// # Returns
160. ///
161. /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
162. ///
163. #[verus_spec(ret =>
164.     ensures
165.         // The frame-allocator invariant is established/preserved on every path: this
166.         // is the precondition every later `frame::*` / `PhysMemoryManager::*` call
167.         // relies on. (Vacuous before the allocator becomes initialized.)
168.         phys_view().inv(),
169.         match ret {
170.             // One-shot boot success: the global subsystem is now initialized and its
171.             // reservation state is well-formed, so reserved frames (allocated) are
172.             // disjoint from the free pool and can never be handed out by `alloc`.
173.             Ok(()) => {
174.                 &&& phys_view().initialized
175.                 &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.disjoint(phys_view().frames.free_frames)
176.             },
177.             // Failure is terminal for the boot path; no completeness of reservation is
178.             // promised, only that the invariant still holds (checked above).
179.             Err(_) => true,
180.         },
181. )]
182. pub fn init(
183.     physical_memory_regions: LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>>,
184.     mmio_regions: &LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<VirtualAddress>>,
185.     physical_memory_layout: Bitmap,
186. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
187.     // Initialize frame allocator singleton.
188.     info!("initializing the frame allocator ...");
189.     // Safety: called exactly once during single-threaded boot.
190.     unsafe { frame::init(physical_memory_layout)? };
191.     book_physical_memory_regions(physical_memory_regions)?;
192. 
193.     book_mmio_regions(mmio_regions)?;
194. 
195.     // Initialize user page pool.
196.     info!("initializing the user page pool ...");
197.     let upool: Upool = Upool::new();
198. 
199.     // Initialize physical memory manager singleton.
200.     info!("initializing the physical memory manager ...");
201.     PhysMemoryManager::init(upool)?;
202. 
203.     Ok(())
204. }
205.

207. // Standalone Functions
208. //==================================================================================================
209.

211. pub fn test() -> bool {
212.     let mut passed = true;
213. 
214.     passed &= test::test();
215. 
216.     passed
217. }

# Build Nanvix

Use this skill when the user asks to build, compile, format, lint, or spell-check Nanvix. This
covers all build-system operations exposed through the `z` utility.

## Prerequisites

- Development environment set up per `doc/setup.md`.
- A local cross-compilation toolchain (`toolchain/`).
- **Windows 11:** GNU Make on PATH, Windows Hypervisor Platform enabled,
  Developer Mode enabled, and Rust toolchain installed. See `doc/setup.md` for details.

## Windows Setup Summary

Before building on Windows, ensure:

1. **Windows Hypervisor Platform** is enabled (`Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName HypervisorPlatform -All`, then reboot).
2. **Developer Mode** is on (Settings > Privacy & Security > For developers).
3. **GNU Make** is on PATH (`winget install ezwinports.make`).
4. **Rust toolchain** is installed via `winget install Rustlang.Rustup`.
5. Repository was cloned with `git clone -c core.symlinks=true`.
6. Git hooks are installed: `./z.ps1 setup`.

## Building

### Preferred Build Commands (using `z` utility)

```bash
# Build everything with the local toolchain.
./z build -- all
```

### Building Individual Components

```bash
# Kernel only.
./z build -- kernel
# Nanvixd only.
./z build -- all-nanvixd
# UserVM only.
./z build -- all-uservm
```

### Build Parameters

Set these as environment variables or pass them after `--` in the `z` command:

| Parameter        | Values                   | Default         |
|------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| `MACHINE`        | `microvm`                | `microvm`       |
| `TARGET`         | `x86`                    | `x86`           |
| `RELEASE`        | `yes`, `no`              | `no`            |
| `LOG_LEVEL`      | `trace`, `debug`,        | `error`         |
|                  | `info`, `warn`,          |                 |
|                  | `error`, `panic`         |                 |
| `PROFILER`       | `yes`, `no`              | `no`            |
| `DEPLOYMENT_MODE`| `standalone`,            | `standalone`    |
|                  | `single-process`,        |                 |
|                  | `multi-process`, `l2`    |                 |

Example with custom parameters:

```bash
./z build -- all RELEASE=yes LOG_LEVEL=error
```

### Manual Build Variants

```bash
# Default debug build.
./z build -- all
# Release build.
./z build -- all RELEASE=yes LOG_LEVEL=panic
# For echo-breakdown benchmark.
./z build -- all RELEASE=yes LOG_LEVEL=panic TIMESTAMP_MSG=yes
```

### Building on Windows (using `z.ps1`)

On Windows 11, the `z.ps1` PowerShell script provides the same CLI interface. Guest components are
cross-compiled using a local toolchain; host binaries (`nanvixd`, `uservm`) are built natively with the
microvm backend (WHP on Windows).

```powershell
# Build everything (guest via make + host binaries natively).
.\z.ps1 build -- all

# Build only the UserVM (native Windows build).
.\z.ps1 build -- uservm

# Build only nanvixd (native Windows build).
.\z.ps1 build -- nanvixd

# Build only nanvix-bench (native Windows build).
.\z.ps1 build -- nanvix-bench

# Build only guest components (kernel + hello-rust-nostd).
.\z.ps1 build -- guest

# Release build.
.\z.ps1 build -- all RELEASE=yes
```

Any unrecognized target is forwarded to `make`, just like on Linux:

```powershell
.\z.ps1 build -- kernel
.\z.ps1 build -- format-check
.\z.ps1 build -- lint-check
```

## Code Quality

### Formatting

```bash
# Check formatting issues.
./z build -- format-check
# Auto-fix formatting issues.
./z build -- format
```

### Linting

```bash
# Check linting issues.
./z build -- lint-check
# Auto-fix linting issues.
./z build -- lint
```

### Spell Checking

```bash
# Check spelling errors.
./z build -- spellcheck
# Fix spelling errors.
./z build -- spellcheck-fix
```

## Formal Verification

Nanvix uses Verus for formal verification of selected kernel crates. The expected Verus version is pinned in `build/verus-version`. Verification requires `VERUS_EXECUTABLE_DIR` to be set; when unset, `make verify` is a no-op.

```bash
# Install verus and run verification.
./scripts/setup/verus.sh ~/toolchain/verus
./z build -- verify VERUS_EXECUTABLE_DIR=~/toolchain/verus

# Verify a single crate.
./z build -- verify-bitmap VERUS_EXECUTABLE_DIR=~/toolchain/verus
```

- Set `VERUS_EXECUTABLE_DIR` to the directory containing the `verus` binary.
- Use `scripts/setup/verus.sh <dir>` to download the pinned release.
- The `vstd` crate version in `Cargo.toml` is exact-pinned (`=`) to match the Verus binary.

## Cleaning

```bash
./z clean        # Clean build artifacts.
./z distclean    # Remove all generated files.
```

### Cleaning on Windows

```powershell
.\z.ps1 clean        # Quick clean (UserVM artifacts + cache).
.\z.ps1 distclean    # Full clean (cargo clean + all artifacts).
```

## CI/CD Pipeline

```bash
# Run the full CI pipeline locally.
./scripts/pipeline.sh
```

The pipeline covers: spell checking, formatting, linting, building, and testing across multiple
machine and deployment configurations.

## IDE Setup (Optional)

### Visual Studio Code

Use the host-specific settings template. The Linux template invokes `./z`, while the Windows
template routes Rust Analyzer through `./z.bat build -- check`, which runs native `cargo check`
on host crates (`uservm`, `nanvixd`, `nanvix-test`, `mkramfs`).

**Linux:**

```bash
mkdir -p .vscode && cd .vscode
ln -s ../scripts/setup/vscode/settings-linux.json settings.json
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path .vscode -Force
Copy-Item scripts\setup\vscode\settings-windows.json .vscode\settings.json
```

> **Note:** The `check` target in `z.ps1` only checks host crates natively. Guest and kernel
> crates require the cross-compilation toolchain. Run
> `.\z.ps1 build -- check-kernel check-guest-binaries` for a full cross-target check.

## Troubleshooting Build Issues

- If builds fail with toolchain errors, verify `toolchain/` symlink points to a valid toolchain.
- Use `./z help` for usage information.
- **Windows:** Use `.\z.ps1 help` for Windows-specific usage information.
- **Windows:** If the UserVM build fails, verify that the Windows Hypervisor Platform feature is
  enabled (`Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName HypervisorPlatform`).
